messages:
maria: Heads-up: deploy-bot rejected an ECR publish for staging (myapi:2026-03-21) citing cosign timestamp in the future (signature_time > server_time). Publish blocked. Anyone know why our build produced a future timestamp?

deploy-bot: publish_rejected: reason=[cosign.signature_time_skew]; details: signature_time=2026-03-22T02:10:15Z, server_time=2026-03-21T23:05:42Z. See https://deploybot.internal/rejects/4412345678

noah: I ran a self-hosted runner in EU and its clock drifted after NTP outage. CI created a signature with the runner's local time. We recently rotated the runners and maybe NTP wasn't configured.

olivia: security: cosign sig with future timestamp invalidates provenance; we can't accept that into prod. For staging we can either re-sign or allowlist this signature time window temporarily. Prefer re-signing.

paul: ops note: we have a short change window in 30m. I'd prefer rollback and re-sign rather than fiddling with allowlists. Rollback canary to previous digest quick.

maria: decision: rollback canary to sha256:11111111... now, then re-run EU runner with corrected NTP and re-sign the image. Also file INFRA-6130 to ensure runners run chronyd and have ntp healthchecks.

deploy-bot: rollback applied by paul: canary now points to sha256:11111111.... health checks pending.

noah: fixed NTP on the EU runners and re-triggered the resign job: `CI_REGION=eu ./ci/cosign-resign.sh --force`. New signature timestamp: 2026-03-21T23:10:05Z.

deploy-bot: publish_check: signature_time within allowed skew. Publish accepted for staging.

maria: updating release notes: "staging publish blocked due to cosign signature clock skew from EU runner NTP outage; rolled back canary and re-signed after fixing runner time; INFRA-6130 opened."

olivia: thanks. Security follow-up: we'll add a CI gate to fail if cosign timestamp > now + 5s and alert on runner NTP drift.

paul: monitoring canary for +30m then resume ramp. If anything odd, escalate.
